name: The Bight, Norman Island
say: The big sheltered bay on Norman Island, the first night out for half the charter fleet. A beach bar at the head of it and a floating one on a mooring.

ashore.name: the Willy T, the floating bar in the Bight
ashore.say: Tie the dinghy astern of the old steel schooner, and somebody jumps off the top deck.

name: The Caves, Treasure Point
say: Three sea caves in the cliff at the south side of the Bight. Day moorings only: swim in with a torch.

ashore.name: the Caves at Treasure Point
ashore.say: Mask and fins over the side, and into the dark of the northern cave among the glassy sweepers.

name: The Indians
say: Four rock pinnacles standing out of deep water off Pelican Island. National park day moorings on the west side.

ashore.name: the reef at the Indians
ashore.say: Round the pinnacles with the parrotfish, through the cut and back to the boat.

name: Wreck of the Rhone, Salt Island
say: The Royal Mail steamer Rhone went on to Black Rock Point in the hurricane of 1867. Marine park moorings over the wreck.

ashore.name: the wreck of the Rhone
ashore.say: Down the mooring line to look: the stern and the great propeller lie in shallow water.

name: Cooper Island
say: Manchioneel Bay, under the lee of Cooper Island. Moorings off the beach club, and turtles in the grass.

ashore.name: the Cooper Island Beach Club
ashore.say: A sundowner on the deck, facing west down the channel toward Tortola.

name: The Baths
say: House-sized granite boulders heaped on the beach at the south end of Virgin Gorda. Day moorings: swim the dinghy line in.

ashore.name: the Baths
ashore.say: Through the grotto between the boulders, wading, and out on to Devil's Bay.

name: Spanish Town
say: Virgin Gorda's town, with the yacht harbour inside the reef. Customs, water and a taxi to the Baths.

ashore.name: the pub at the yacht harbour
ashore.say: Rotis and a cold beer at the bar by the dinghy dock.

name: Leverick Bay
say: The marina on the Virgin Gorda side of North Sound: fuel, water and a beach bar.

ashore.name: the beach bar at Leverick Bay
ashore.say: Barbecue on the sand and the stilt-walkers come out after dark.

name: Bitter End
say: The far end of North Sound, reached only by water. A big mooring field under the hill.

ashore.name: the Bitter End Yacht Club
ashore.say: A rum at the quarterdeck bar, watching the dinghies race round the moorings.

name: Saba Rock
say: An acre of rock in the gap between Bitter End and Prickly Pear, all of it a bar and a few rooms.

ashore.name: the bar on Saba Rock
ashore.say: Happy hour on the terrace, and the tarpon come to be fed under the dock lights.

name: Trellis Bay
say: A round bay on Beef Island beside the airport, with Bellamy Cay in the middle of it.

ashore.name: the beach at Trellis Bay
ashore.say: Fire balls burning in the shallows and a band on the sand: it is full moon.

name: Marina Cay
say: A speck of an island behind its own reef, between Beef Island and Great Camanoe.

ashore.name: the bar on Marina Cay
ashore.say: A walk round the whole island in ten minutes, then a drink at the top of it.

name: Cane Garden Bay
say: A mile of palm beach on Tortola's north shore, under the hills. Rolly when a north swell runs.

ashore.name: Quito's Gazebo, on the beach
ashore.say: Live music over the water and your feet in the sand.

name: Great Harbour, Jost Van Dyke
say: Jost Van Dyke's village: a sand street, a customs house and a row of beach bars.

ashore.name: Foxy's, at the east end of the beach
ashore.say: Foxy is on the guitar, making up a calypso about wherever you say you are from.

name: White Bay, Jost Van Dyke
say: A white beach behind a reef, a short walk over the hill from Great Harbour. There is no dock: you swim ashore.

ashore.name: the Soggy Dollar Bar
ashore.say: Pay with wet notes for a Painkiller with nutmeg grated on top.

name: Sandy Cay
say: An uninhabited island of sand and palms east of Jost Van Dyke. Anchor in sand under its lee, by day.

ashore.name: the beach on Sandy Cay
ashore.say: Round the island by the trail through the trees, and nobody else on it.

name: Sandy Spit
say: A sand bar with a few palms off Green Cay, the desert island of the postcards.

ashore.name: Sandy Spit
ashore.say: Thirty paces from one side to the other, and the yacht in the picture behind you.

name: Soper's Hole
say: The harbour at Tortola's West End, between Frenchman's Cay and the shore. Ferries, customs and painted wharf houses.

ashore.name: the wharf at Soper's Hole
ashore.say: Coffee and provisions among the pink and blue wharf houses.

name: Road Town
say: The capital, at the head of Road Harbour. Charter bases, chandlers and the customs dock.

ashore.name: the waterfront at Road Town
ashore.say: A pub lunch on the waterfront and the shopping list done.

name: Nanny Cay
say: A marina and boatyard on its own cay, west of Road Town. Home of the spring regatta.

ashore.name: the beach bar at Nanny Cay
ashore.say: A swim off the marina beach and a burger at the bar.
